blocks.title: <ico-recycle></ico-recycle> REPASO EXPRESS · lección anterior
blocks.intro: Antes de empezar, recupera lo de la clase pasada. Une cada expresión con su significado, sin mirar atrás.

blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> ROSE SHARPLY vs A SHARP RISE
blocks.intro: Una presentación tiene tres partes y cada una se abre con una frase fija. Y los números no se leen: se cuentan como tendencias, con verbo + adverbio o con adjetivo + sustantivo.

vocab.en: Let me start with a question.
As you can see on this chart,…
vocab.sp: como pueden ver en este gráfico,…

vocab.en: Let's take a look at the numbers.
This brings me to my next point.
vocab.sp: esto me lleva al siguiente punto

vocab.en: a rise / a fall / a drop
vocab.sp: una subida / una caída / una baja
con eso termina la primera parte

blocks.note: Cómo funciona: tarjetas , memory, escucha , comparar , completar y ordenar . CHECK donde lo veas.

parts.html: 1 · TRES PARTES, TRES FRASES — abrir, cambiar de tema, cerrar

items.en: Today I'd like to walk you through our plan.
items.sp: Abrir: dices de qué vas a hablar.
Cambiar de tema: avisas que empieza otra parte.

items.en: To sum up, phase two is on track.

parts.html: 2 · SUBE, BAJA, SE MANTIENE — los verbos de tendencia

items.sp: Los pedidos subieron en primavera. (rise · rose · risen)
Los costos bajaron el trimestre pasado. (fall · fell · fallen)

items.en: Sales leveled off in the summer.
items.sp: Las ventas se estabilizaron en verano.

parts.html: 3 · ¿CUÁNTO Y QUÉ TAN RÁPIDO? — el adverbio va después del verbo

items.sp: Crecieron poco a poco, sin parar.

parts.html: 4 · DALE LA VUELTA — verbo + adverbio ↔ adjetivo + sustantivo

items.en: There was a sharp rise in sales.
There was steady growth in orders.
There was a slight fall in costs.

parts.body: El adverbio pierde el -ly y pasa adelante: rose sharply → a sharp rise. Después del sustantivo va in: a rise of sales → a rise in sales.

parts.html: 5 · BY, TO, FROM, AT — la preposición cambia el dato

items.sp: at = el punto más alto (o el nivel donde se quedan).

parts.html: TRAMPA DEL ESPAÑOL — cuatro errores típicos al presentar

items.en: Thank you for attending this presentation.
I'm going to present our results.
items.sp: «Exponer» = present. Expose es dejar algo al descubierto.

items.en: Prices rose, so we raised our salaries.
items.sp: rise: algo sube solo. raise: tú lo subes.

parts.body: Sales grew a 20%. → Sales grew by 20%. · We rose our prices. → We raised our prices.

blocks.title: PRESENTATION WORDS · toca para girar
blocks.intro: Diez palabras para guiar a tu público. Las vas a escuchar en los dos audios.

blocks.title: <ico-star></ico-star> THE EXPANSION PLAN
blocks.intro: Primer trabajo de Marcos como líder interino: presentar la fase dos de GreenMarket ante la junta directiva de David. La noche anterior, Sofia lo escucha ensayar… y lo detiene en la primera diapositiva.

blocks.title: MEMORY · the phrase and its job
blocks.intro: Cada frase tiene un trabajo dentro de la presentación. Toca dos cartas y encuentra las parejas.

pairs.b: dar el mapa de la charla

pairs.a: I'll take questions at the end.

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE DRY RUN
blocks.desc: La noche antes: Marcos ensaya frente a Sofia y lee sus diapositivas una por una. Ella le arregla el comienzo y los números.

questions.q: What was wrong with Marcos's opening?
Which phrase does Sofia give him to change topic?
options: Let me walk you through three things.

questions.q: What is the corrected number sentence?
How does Marcos feel at the end?

speaking.prompt: Give Marcos's new opening yourself: a hook question, then the three-part map.
speaking.starter: What if I told you (surprising fact)? Today I'd like to walk you through three things: (1), (2) and (3).

transcript.html: Okay, Sofia, here goes. "Good morning. My name is Marcos. This presentation is about GreenMarket phase two. Slide one. In January, we had two thousand orders. In June, we had three thousand five hundred orders. In…"
Stop, stop. Marcos, you're reading your slides. The board can read. Start with a hook, a question, and then give them the map.

Something like: "What if I told you GreenMarket could double its orders in one year?" Then the map: "Today I'd like to walk you through three things: where we are, where we're going, and what we need from you."
Okay, I like that. And the numbers?
Don't list them. Tell me the trend. What happened between January and June?
Orders went from two thousand to three thousand five hundred. A little more every month.
So say it like a story: "Orders rose steadily from two thousand to three thousand five hundred."
"Orders rose steadily from two thousand to three thousand five hundred." That does sound better.
Much better. And when you change topic, don't just say "slide two." Say "Moving on to the budget."
"Moving on to the budget." Got it. You know, an hour ago I wanted to call in sick tomorrow. Now I think I want to do this.
Good. One more run, and then go home and sleep.

blocks.title: ROSE SHARPLY vs A SHARP RISE
blocks.intro: El mismo dato, dicho de dos formas. Mira qué palabra cambia de forma al pasar de una a la otra.

pair.b: There was a sharp rise in sales.

options: No: A es una subida más grande

items.q: En B, ¿en qué se convierte el verbo «rose»?
Di de otra forma: «Costs fell slightly.»
options: There was a slightly fall in costs.
There was a slight fall in costs.
There was a slight fall of costs.

items.q: Di de otra forma: «There was steady growth in orders.»

blocks.title: THE RIGHT WORD FOR THE CHART
blocks.intro: Elige la preposición o la forma correcta (adverbio, adjetivo o verbo).

items.q: There was a ___ drop in costs.
There was a slight rise ___ prices.
After a strong spring, sales ___ in the summer.

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · THE REAL THING
blocks.desc: Al día siguiente, frente a la junta de David: el comienzo ya pulido, con un gráfico de pedidos del año.

questions.q: How many things does Marcos say he will cover?
Why did orders dip in August?
When did orders peak, and at what number?

speaking.prompt: Describe the same chart in four sentences: the rise, the dip, the peak, and one sentence to sum up.
speaking.starter: Orders rose (adverb) from (number) to (number). In August, they (verb + adverb). They peaked at (number) in (month). To sum up, (key takeaway).

transcript.html: Good morning, everyone. What if I told you that GreenMarket could double its orders in one year? Well, it already has. Today I'd like to walk you through three things: where we are, where we're going, and what we need from you. Let's start with where we are. As you can see on this chart, orders rose steadily from two thousand in January to five thousand in July. They dipped slightly in August, when many customers were on vacation, and then they climbed again. In November, orders peaked at six thousand two hundred. That is a rise of more than two hundred percent in eleven months. To sum up the first part: growth has been strong and steady, and the summer dip was small. I'll take questions at the end. Now, moving on to where we're going. In phase two, we plan to open in three new cities.

blocks.title: <ico-pen></ico-pen> MY 60 SECONDS
blocks.intro: Escribe el primer minuto de una presentación sobre tu trabajo, tu proyecto o tu ciudad (6–8 frases). Inventa los números si hace falta.
checklist: Empieza con una pregunta que enganche (What if I told you…? / Did you know that…?)
Da el mapa en tres partes (Today I'd like to walk you through…)
Un dato como verbo + adverbio (rose sharply) y el mismo como adjetivo + sustantivo (a sharp rise in…)
Preposiciones correctas: by / to / from… to… / at
blocks.example: pregunta gancho? Today I'd like to walk you through tema. First, parte 1. Then, parte 2. Finally, parte 3. As you can see, qué verbo + adverbio from número to número. In other words, there was a adjetivo + sustantivo in qué. To sum up, idea clave.
blocks.hw: Escribe tu minuto y después grábate presentándolo de pie, sin leer, en 60 segundos. Envíame texto y audio por WhatsApp.

rubric.d: Escribiste el número de frases que pide la consigna: gancho, mapa, dato y cierre.
Describiste la tendencia de las dos formas (verbo + adverbio y adjetivo + sustantivo) con la preposición correcta.
Un lector lo entiende sin releer: ideas unidas con conectores, sin traducir literal del español.
